body:
# Theming — architecture + migration plan

Design doc for filemark's theming + CSS distribution model. Locks the architecture before we refactor existing CSS out of the apps into the packages.

- **Date opened:** 2026-04-24
- **Owner:** personal
- **Scope:** refactor of `.fv-*` CSS across `packages/*` + `apps/{chrome-ext,playground}`
- **Deps:** decision in this doc; no new packages unless explicitly listed

---

## 1. Goals

- **Every filemark package publishable standalone to npm.** Consumer installs `@filemark/tasks`, imports one CSS file, styles work.
- **Zero CSS duplication between `apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css` and `apps/playground/src/styles.css`.** Both apps import the same source from packages; app-local stylesheets carry only shadcn tokens + Tailwind imports.
- **Themable via CSS variables at ~50 documented tokens.** A third party writes `html[data-theme="brand-b"] { --fm-tone-danger: ...; }` and every component re-skins with zero component rebuild.
- **Plays with existing shadcn theming** (`data-theme="light|dark|sepia"`) without conflict or overlap.
- **No runtime CSS-in-JS, no build-time magic.** Plain CSS + CSS custom properties. Every browser + bundler supports it.

---

## 2. Non-goals

- **New shared package (`@filemark/styles` / `@filemark/tokens`).** Overhead not justified at current package count (4 that emit styled markup). Revisit if we hit 10+.
- **Runtime theme SDK** (`applyTheme(tokens)` helper). Maybe later; not required for v1. Consumers can roll a 10-line helper from scratch.
- **Overriding Tailwind utilities used for layout.** `flex`, `gap`, `px-2`, `rounded-md` stay inline. Themers override colors / fonts / radii / spacing scale, not structural layout.
- **Dark-mode auto-switching logic.** `data-theme` is set by the consumer app; filemark never inspects `prefers-color-scheme` on its own.
- **Visual regression test infrastructure.** Useful but deferred — out of scope for this refactor.

---

## 3. The theming contract

**A theme is a block of CSS variable overrides scoped under a `data-theme` attribute selector.** One line activates it. Every filemark component reads variables via `var(--fm-*, fallback)` — no component code touched.

```css
html[data-theme="brand-b"] {
  --fm-tone-danger:  oklch(0.7 0.3 300);   /* purple instead of red */
  --fm-chip-radius:  4px;                   /* square chips */
  --fm-prose-font:   Georgia, serif;
}
```

```ts
document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "brand-b");
```

Done.

---

## 4. Variable-definition strategy — fallbacks at usage sites

**No `:root` token-default block inside any filemark package's CSS.** Every variable is consumed via `var(--fm-X, <fallback>)` where the fallback is **either a shadcn token reference** (`var(--destructive)`, `var(--muted)`, `var(--primary)`) or a **literal value** for filemark-specific knobs with no shadcn counterpart.

Why:
- Consumer using a single filemark package standalone (no mdx) still gets correct styling — fallback kicks in.
- No duplicate `:root` blocks across packages → no drift risk when defaults evolve.
- Theme author overrides **only** the vars they care about; everything else inherits sane defaults.
- "Default filemark theme" = shadcn's palette + a few filemark-specific neutrals. One source of truth.

Example:

```css
/* @filemark/mdx/styles.css */
.fv-chip--danger {
  color:       var(--fm-tone-danger, var(--destructive));
  background:  color-mix(in oklab, var(--fm-tone-danger, var(--destructive)) 15%, transparent);
  border-color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--fm-tone-danger, var(--destructive)) 35%, transparent);
}
.fv-chip {
  padding:       var(--fm-chip-padding, 1px 7px);
  border-radius: var(--fm-chip-radius, 9999px);
  font-size:     var(--fm-chip-font-size, 10.5px);
}
```

Where literals appear in fallbacks, they appear **exactly once per file** for each variable. Grepping `--fm-chip-radius` finds every relevant site.

---

## 5. Variable naming convention

- Prefix **`--fm-`** on every filemark-specific token. Distinct from shadcn's unprefixed tokens (`--primary`, `--muted`) and Tailwind's `--color-*`.
- Semantic family first, then variant: `--fm-tone-danger`, `--fm-chip-radius`, `--fm-prose-font`, `--fm-timeline-bar-radius`.
- Multi-word names use kebab-case inside the family: `--fm-prose-max-width`, `--fm-table-row-padding-compact`.
- Boolean toggles use `--fm-<family>-<enable>`: e.g. `--fm-prose-heading-border: 1px` (set to `0` to disable).

---

## 6. Token catalog — the full `--fm-*` surface

This is the **public theming contract**. Users override any subset. Every variable has a fallback inline at its usage site.

### 6.1 Semantic tones (status / priority / owner chips)

| Variable | Fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--fm-tone-success` | `oklch(0.7 0.15 160)` | done / success chips, safe states |
| `--fm-tone-warn` | `oklch(0.82 0.17 85)` | P1, today/tomorrow, caution |
| `--fm-tone-danger` | `var(--destructive)` | P0, overdue, blocked |
| `--fm-tone-info` | `oklch(0.7 0.16 240)` | P2, upcoming, informational |
| `--fm-tone-owner` | `oklch(0.7 0.17 290)` | `@owner` accent (distinct from priority) |
| `--fm-tone-muted` | `var(--muted-foreground)` | cancelled / deprecated / neutral |
| `--fm-tone-project` | `var(--primary)` | project chips, background accents |

### 6.2 Chip geometry

| Variable | Fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--fm-chip-radius` | `9999px` | pill (default) vs. square (`4px`) |
| `--fm-chip-padding` | `1px 7px` | inside chip |
| `--fm-chip-font-size` | `10.5px` | chip typography |
| `--fm-chip-font-weight` | `500` | chip weight |
| `--fm-chip-border-width` | `1px` | chip border |

### 6.3 Prose / markdown-body typography

| Variable | Fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--fm-prose-font` | `system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif` | body font |
| `--fm-prose-font-size` | `16px` | base size |
| `--fm-prose-line-height` | `1.65` | reading line height |
| `--fm-prose-max-width` | `760px` | reading measure |
| `--fm-prose-heading-weight` | `650` | heading weight |
| `--fm-prose-heading-border` | `1px` | h1/h2 bottom border; `0` disables |
| `--fm-prose-link-color` | `var(--primary)` | link color |
| `--fm-prose-blockquote-bg` | `var(--muted)` | blockquote background |
| `--fm-prose-code-bg` | `var(--muted)` | inline code background |
| `--fm-prose-code-font` | `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace` | inline + block code font |

### 6.4 Table options (`<MDXTable>`)

| Variable | Fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--fm-table-row-padding-compact` | `2px 8px` | compact density |
| `--fm-table-row-padding-cozy` | `6px 12px` | cozy density (default) |
| `--fm-table-row-padding-relaxed` | `12px 16px` | relaxed density |
| `--fm-table-header-bg` | `var(--muted)` | thead bg |
| `--fm-table-zebra-bg` | `color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted) 50%, transparent)` | alternating rows |
| `--fm-table-border-color` | `var(--border)` | cell borders |
| `--fm-table-resize-handle` | `color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 60%, transparent)` | resize grabbers |

### 6.5 Callout / Details / Tabs

| Variable | Fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--fm-callout-border-width` | `3px` | left-edge stripe |
| `--fm-callout-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | rounded corners |
| `--fm-callout-padding` | `0.8em 1em` | inside spacing |
| `--fm-details-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | `<Details>` corners |
| `--fm-tabs-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | `<Tabs>` corners |

### 6.6 Timeline (`<TaskTimeline>`)

| Variable | Fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--fm-timeline-bar-radius` | `3px` | rectangle corner radius |
| `--fm-timeline-bar-height-fraction` | `0.72` | bar height as fraction of row height |
| `--fm-timeline-today-color` | `var(--primary)` | today marker line |
| `--fm-timeline-today-dash` | `3,3` | dash pattern for today line |
| `--fm-timeline-lane-label-width` | `100px` | left lane column width |
| `--fm-timeline-row-height` | `28px` | per-task row height |

### 6.7 Kanban (`<Kanban md>` + `<Kanban src=>`)

| Variable | Fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--fm-kanban-column-min-width` | `260px` | minimum column width |
| `--fm-kanban-column-max-width` | `300px` | maximum column width |
| `--fm-kanban-column-bg` | `var(--card)` | column background |
| `--fm-kanban-card-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | card corner radius |
| `--fm-kanban-card-shadow` | `0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05)` | card shadow |

### 6.8 ADR

| Variable | Fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--fm-adr-body-line-height` | `1.6` | ADR body text |
| `--fm-adr-padding` | `1.2em 1.4em` | ADR inside spacing |
| `--fm-adr-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | corner radius |

### 6.9 Task row / inline chips

| Variable | Fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--fm-task-chip-gap` | `4px` | spacing between inline chips |
| `--fm-task-chip-wrap-margin` | `8px` | left margin between text + chips |
| `--fm-task-flash-color` | `color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 18%, transparent)` | click-to-scroll highlight bg |
| `--fm-task-flash-duration` | `600ms` | fade-out transition |

### 6.10 SmartImage / SmartLink

| Variable | Fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--fm-image-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | image corner radius |
| `--fm-image-border` | `1px solid var(--border)` | image border |

Estimated total: **~55 variables** across 10 families. Each family is independent — override any subset.

---

## 7. Per-package file layout

### 7.1 `@filemark/mdx` — the flagship CSS surface

```
packages/mdx-viewer/
├── package.json           — add "./styles.css" to exports
├── tsup.config.ts         — copy src/styles.css → dist/styles.css
└── src/
    ├── styles.css         — NEW: consolidated filemark CSS
    │                        • `.fv-mdx-body` typography (library-owned DOM)
    │                        • `.fv-chip` + `.fv-chip--*` themable variants
    │                        • `.fv-mdx-table-*` table options
    │                        • `.fv-task-chips` / `.fv-task-flash`
    │                        • `.fv-callout*` / `.fv-details*` / `.fv-tabs*`
    │                        • `.fv-code-*` inline/block code
    │                        • No `:root` block — fallbacks at usage sites
    └── index.ts           — unchanged
```

Export:

```json
"exports": {
  ".":             { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js" },
  "./styles.css":  "./dist/styles.css"
}
```

### 7.2 `@filemark/tasks`, `@filemark/kanban`, `@filemark/datagrid`, `@filemark/chart`

These have visuals but today are mostly Tailwind-inline. **No separate `styles.css` needed** unless a component uses a `.fv-*` class name. Review case-by-case:

- `@filemark/datagrid` — `TONE_CLASS` inline Tailwind. **No CSS file needed.**
- `@filemark/kanban` — Board/Column/Card Tailwind inline. **No CSS file needed.**
- `@filemark/chart` — recharts-driven SVG. **No CSS file needed.**
- `@filemark/tasks` — pure logic (parser + context + predicates). **No CSS file needed.** Visual components live in `@filemark/mdx`.

Decision: **only `@filemark/mdx` ships a `styles.css` file for v1**. If a future sibling package adds `.fv-*` markup, it gets its own `styles.css` following the same no-`:root`-with-fallbacks pattern.

### 7.3 `apps/chrome-ext` + `apps/playground`

Both shrink dramatically:

```
apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css
  — keeps shadcn :root tokens (--background, --primary, --destructive, etc.)
  — keeps Tailwind imports + @source scanning
  — keeps dark / sepia theme overrides
  — imports @filemark/mdx/styles.css
  — DELETES all .fv-* blocks

apps/playground/src/styles.css
  — same shape, same import, no .fv-* duplication
```

A consumer's `main.tsx` only needs to add one line:

```ts
import "@filemark/mdx/styles.css";
```

---

## 8. Class-name normalization

Current mix is inconsistent. Part of this refactor: normalize every filemark class to a stable prefix.

- **`.fv-chip` + `.fv-chip--<tone>`** — the shared chip family. Used by `TaskChips` (inline), `TaskPanel` (side panel), `TaskList` (rows), `KanbanFromTasks` (cards). Today split as `.fv-task-chip*` — **rename to `.fv-chip*`** so non-task consumers can use it too.
- **`.fv-mdx-body`** + descendants — stays as is (matches existing convention).
- **`.fv-mdx-table-*`** — stays.
- **`.fv-callout*` / `.fv-details*` / `.fv-tabs*`** — stay.

After normalization, every class in the shipped CSS starts with `fv-` and follows `fv-<component>` or `fv-<component>--<variant>` BEM-ish style.

---

## 9. Consumer usage — three scenarios

### 9.1 Consumer app (filemark internal)

```ts
// apps/chrome-ext/src/main.tsx
import "@filemark/mdx/styles.css";
// optional theme override above or below
import "./theme-brand-b.css";
```

Zero `.fv-*` blocks in app CSS; only app-specific shadcn tokens.

### 9.2 External npm consumer

```sh
npm install @filemark/mdx
```

```ts
// consumer-app/src/main.tsx
import "@filemark/mdx/styles.css";
```

Works. Optionally add their own theme CSS file.

### 9.3 Theme author publishing on npm

```
filemark-theme-neon/
├── package.json
└── theme.css    — single file with html[data-theme="neon"] { --fm-*: ...; }
```

Consumer:

```ts
import "@filemark/mdx/styles.css";
import "filemark-theme-neon/theme.css";
document.documentElement.dataset.theme = "neon";
```

---

## 10. Migration plan — step-by-step

Total scope: ~10 file edits. No new packages.

### Step 1 — build the CSS file

Create `packages/mdx-viewer/src/styles.css`. Consolidate from:
- `apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css` — all `.fv-*` blocks
- `apps/playground/src/styles.css` — same (identical duplicate)

Transform: swap every hardcoded color / radius / padding to `var(--fm-*, fallback)`. No `:root` block in this file.

### Step 2 — wire tsup

`packages/mdx-viewer/tsup.config.ts`:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  entry: ["src/index.ts"],
  format: ["esm"],
  dts: true,
  sourcemap: true,
  clean: true,
  external: [...],
  loader: { ".css": "copy" },
  // Copy styles.css to dist/
  onSuccess: "cp src/styles.css dist/styles.css",
  target: "es2022",
  splitting: false,
});
```

(Or use tsup's built-in asset copy if available; `onSuccess` works everywhere.)

### Step 3 — add package.json export

```json
{
  "exports": {
    ".":            { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js" },
    "./styles.css": "./dist/styles.css"
  },
  "files": ["dist"]
}
```

### Step 4 — rename `.fv-task-chip*` → `.fv-chip*` across components

Files touching chips:
- `packages/mdx-viewer/src/components/TaskItem.tsx`
- `packages/mdx-viewer/src/components/TaskList.tsx`
- `packages/mdx-viewer/src/components/KanbanFromTasks.tsx`
- `apps/chrome-ext/src/app/shell/TaskPanel.tsx`

Simple find-and-replace. Container `.fv-task-chips` also renames to `.fv-chips` (or stays — it's not a tone variant, bikeshed later).

### Step 5 — strip app stylesheets

`apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css`:
- Delete every `.fv-*` rule block
- Keep shadcn tokens + Tailwind imports + dark/sepia overrides

`apps/playground/src/styles.css`: same.

### Step 6 — import the CSS once in each app entry

`apps/chrome-ext/src/main.tsx`:
```ts
import "@filemark/mdx/styles.css";
import "./styles/index.css";
```

`apps/playground/src/main.tsx`: same pattern.

### Step 7 — typecheck + build + eyeball

```sh
pnpm -r typecheck
pnpm -r build
```

Reload the chrome-ext + the playground. Every `.fv-*` class should still render correctly — identical look via fallbacks.

### Step 8 — publish the theming doc

Copy this file's §6 (token catalog) into the `@filemark/mdx` README or a `THEMING.md` sibling in the package. Ship with the npm release.

### Step 9 — seed a test theme

Add `examples/themes/neon.css` to the repo demonstrating an end-to-end override — proves the theming contract works in practice. Loads conditionally in the playground via a URL param (e.g., `?theme=neon`).

---

## 11. Validation criteria

Before declaring done:

- [ ] `@filemark/mdx` built; `dist/styles.css` exists and is the consolidated file
- [ ] `@filemark/mdx/styles.css` import works in a fresh consumer context (test via `vite build` on a minimal repo)
- [ ] chrome-ext renders identically before + after (visual diff on `examples/tasks-full.md`)
- [ ] playground renders identically before + after
- [ ] adding `html[data-theme="neon"] { --fm-tone-danger: ...; }` actually changes the danger chip color everywhere
- [ ] token catalog in §6 matches every `--fm-*` usage in the CSS (grep audit)
- [ ] no file anywhere in `packages/*` contains a `:root { --fm-*: ...; }` block

---

## 12. Future work (post v1)

- **Formal `apply()` helper** — `applyTheme(name, tokens)` exported from `@filemark/mdx` for dynamic theme builders. Maybe 15 lines of code; skip until a consumer asks.
- **Theme linter** — CI script that verifies every `--fm-*` usage has a matching catalog entry, and vice versa.
- **Per-subpackage CSS files** if a subpackage ever emits `.fv-*` markup of its own (e.g., a future `@filemark/form` with its own chip shapes).
- **Visual regression tests** — Playwright screenshots before/after theme change.
- **Named theme catalog on npm** — community-published themes: `filemark-theme-solarized`, `filemark-theme-dracula`, etc.
- **Interactive theme builder** in filemark's options page — user picks colors, sees live preview, exports as a CSS file.

---

## 13. Open questions

1. **Should `.fv-task-chips` container class rename too?** Consistency says yes (`.fv-chips`). But `.fv-chips` is a very generic name — risk of collision with consumer CSS. Propose: keep `.fv-task-chips` for the in-document inline container; use `.fv-chip` for the actual chip element.
2. **Should we document the `--fm-*` token defaults in code or in this doc?** Proposal: this doc is canonical for defaults, fallbacks inline in the CSS file are the implementation. CI lint ensures they match.
3. **Should the css file live at `packages/mdx-viewer/src/styles.css` or `packages/mdx-viewer/styles.css`?** tsup convention suggests `src/`; keeping source inside `src/` stays consistent with other package entries. Going with `src/styles.css` → `dist/styles.css`.
4. **Chip sizing — fixed px or `em` relative to prose font size?** Current: fixed `10.5px`. Consider: `0.66em` so chips scale with `--fm-prose-font-size`. Defer — pick one when we actually want scaling.
5. **Dark-mode defaults for `--fm-tone-*`** — the shipped CSS currently has `[data-theme="dark"]` overrides for each tone (brighter / less saturated to work on dark bg). In the new model, do we (a) ship a `[data-theme="dark"]` block with filemark-specific overrides, or (b) rely on shadcn's dark overrides of `--destructive` / `--primary` which we fall through to? Leaning (a) — filemark's own semantic palette needs its own dark-mode tuning.

---

## 14. Related docs

- `docsi/ARCHITECTURE.md` — component pipeline overview (where `.fv-*` classes come from).
- `docsi/TASKS_PLAN.md` §19.3 — documents the current CSS duplication problem; this doc supersedes it with a fix.
- `apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css` — current source of `.fv-*` blocks; will shrink dramatically.
- `apps/playground/src/styles.css` — same.
- `packages/mdx-viewer/src/components/*.tsx` — every component that will rename `.fv-task-chip*` → `.fv-chip*`.
